topic: Hot take: Microsoft offers buyouts to ~60,000 employees as AI spending climbs
post:
Microsoft just offered about 60,000 employees money to leave. 💼
My hot take: "voluntary" is the new way AI reshapes a company.

What's been reported 👇
👥 The voluntary exit offer covers about a quarter of Microsoft's workforce
🌍 It's for eligible teams in the US, UK, Canada and India
💵 Microsoft says the package is comparable to its standard severance
🏗️ Coverage ties it to a big ramp-up in AI data center spending
📌 GeekWire notes it isn't a replacement for layoffs

Here's my take:
Big companies are learning they can reshape a workforce without the headline of a mass layoff. Pay people to choose, then redirect the money to AI.

The catch? The people most likely to say yes are often the ones with the best options elsewhere.

Why it matters:
The AI shift won't always look like layoffs. Sometimes it looks like a polite offer, a reorg, or a role that quietly isn't backfilled. 🔍

Practical takeaway:
Don't wait for an offer to decide your plan. Write down this week what makes you hard to replace, and what AI skill would make you harder. 📝

Would you take a buyout if you were offered one? 👇

Follow for daily AI news you can actually use.
